description: What standalone emulators' own loaders take — Dolphin's and PrimeHack's (#618), PCSX2's, PPSSPP's and DuckStation's (#744): whole fixture machines in, the launchability verdict of each such entry out — judged by the loader cards read at the builds RetroDECK ships, for the command shapes those cards were read for.

vectors.name: dolphin-a-zip-on-wii-is-not-accepted-by-the-dolphin-entry
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK's wii list declares .zip on account of every entry, and the entry the frontend puts first is Dolphin's own: its loader takes a file by extension and holds no branch for an archive, so the zip is refused and the verdict is entry-not-accepted. PrimeHack refuses it the same way and the libretro entry's core was not read, so no entry is established to take it.

vectors.name: emudeck-dolphin-with-the-upstream-prefix-refuses-a-zip
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck's ES-DE runs its own catalogue, whose Dolphin entry opens with an %INJECT% of a per-game prefix file: that text is placed in front of the emulator, and Dolphin is still handed -b -e %ROM%, so the card answers — the zip is refused.

vectors.name: emudeck-dolphin-on-consolearcade-takes-an-iso-with-its-content-unread
vectors.rationale: ES-DE's consolearcade system declares a Dolphin entry of the same shape; named by its label, it takes an .iso by its extension, with the content unread.

/home/deck/Applications/ES-DE.AppImage.usr/share/es-de/resources/systems/linux/:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<systemList>
  <system>
    <name>consolearcade</name>
    <path>%ROMPATH%/consolearcade</path>
    <extension>.arcadedef .desktop .iso .ISO .ps3 .PS3 .sh .xbe .XBE .7z .7Z .zip .ZIP</extension>
    <command label="MAME - Current">%EMULATOR_RETROARCH% -L %CORE_RETROARCH%/mame_libretro.so %ROM%</command>
    <command label="Dolphin">%EMULATOR_RETROARCH% -L %CORE_RETROARCH%/dolphin_libretro.so %ROM%</command>
    <command label="Dolphin (Standalone)">%INJECT%=%BASENAME%.esprefix %EMULATOR_DOLPHIN% -b -e %ROM%</command>
    <command label="Triforce (Standalone)">%INJECT%=%BASENAME%.esprefix %EMULATOR_TRIFORCE% -b -e %ROM%</command>
  </system>
</systemList>

vectors.name: pcsx2-an-iso-is-launchable-with-its-content-unread
vectors.rationale: PCSX2's CLI boots the file it is handed with no extension check, and its reader for an .iso is the flat one; whether the image holds a disc is read from its sectors, which atlas does not read, so the take states entry-format-content-unread.

vectors.name: pcsx2-an-ngr-is-read-as-a-flat-image
vectors.rationale: The ps2 list spells .ngr beside .NRG, so the frontend scans a .ngr. PCSX2 reads every extension it names no reader for as a flat image, this one too, so the card takes it with the content unread.

vectors.name: pcsx2-a-lower-case-nrg-the-list-does-not-name-is-read
vectors.rationale: The ps2 accept-list carries .ngr and .NRG but not .nrg, so ES-DE never lists Game.nrg. PCSX2's loader compares the extension without case and reads an .nrg as a flat image, so the entry takes the file: launchable, with the frontend's naming stated beside it rather than as the verdict (#776 D1, D2).

vectors.name: pcsx2-an-upper-case-nrg-is-launchable-as-its-loader-folds-case
vectors.rationale: The list's .NRG is matched by the card's .nrg: PCSX2 compares extensions without case.

vectors.name: pcsx2-a-zip-is-not-accepted-by-the-pcsx2-entry
vectors.rationale: Neither ES-DE's nor RetroDECK's ps2 list carries .zip; this catalogue adds it. PCSX2 opens no archive: a .zip goes to the flat reader unopened, no disc is found in it, and the BIOS boots with no game. The card refuses it.

vectors.name: pcsx2-a-ciso-is-not-accepted-by-the-pcsx2-entry
vectors.rationale: A .ciso is read as a flat image, not decompressed, so PCSX2 finds no disc in it and boots its BIOS with no game. The card refuses it.

vectors.name: pcsx2-a-playlist-is-not-accepted-by-the-pcsx2-entry
vectors.rationale: PCSX2 reads an .m3u as a flat image, not as a list, and a list of under 17 sectors fails the start. The card refuses it.

vectors.name: pcsx2-a-command-of-another-shape-stays-unestablished
vectors.rationale: The card was read for -batch %ROM%; an entry handing PCSX2 the file without -batch is one the card does not answer for.

vectors.name: ppsspp-an-iso-is-launchable-with-its-content-unread
vectors.rationale: PPSSPP identifies the file by its bytes, which atlas does not read, so the take states entry-format-content-unread.

vectors.name: ppsspp-a-folder-holding-an-eboot-starts-by-it
vectors.rationale: PPSSPP takes a directory holding EBOOT.PBP as a game and boots that file (Core/Loaders.cpp:87-93, :283-291 at fa50bb19): the entry starts the folder, the source says by what, and the EBOOT.PBP is named as the file it would take on its own (#776 D5).

vectors.name: ppsspp-a-folder-holding-neither-name-is-refused
vectors.rationale: A directory with no EBOOT.PBP and no PSP_GAME inside is 'Just a directory.' to PPSSPP (Core/System.cpp:236 at fa50bb19), so the entry does not start it (#776 D5).

vectors.name: ppsspp-a-folder-that-cannot-be-listed-is-not-established
vectors.rationale: ES-DE builds %ROM% for a directory by looking inside it for a file of its own name (FileData.cpp:1027-1043 at v3.4.1), and this one cannot be listed, so what the entry would be handed cannot be told: unestablished, with launch-path-unestablished (#776 D9).

vectors.name: ppsspp-a-zip-is-launchable-with-its-contents-unread
vectors.rationale: PPSSPP opens a ZIP itself and boots the first .iso, .cso or .chd at most one folder deep, failing the boot where none is there: inside the archive, which atlas does not read, so the take states archive-contents-unread instead of entry-format-content-unread.

vectors.name: ppsspp-an-upper-case-zip-is-launchable-with-its-contents-unread
vectors.rationale: The list's .ZIP is the same archive to PPSSPP, which lowercases the extension.

vectors.name: ppsspp-a-7z-is-not-accepted-by-the-ppsspp-entry
vectors.rationale: PPSSPP identifies a 7z archive by its magic and never boots it, so the card refuses .7z.

vectors.name: ppsspp-a-command-of-another-shape-stays-unestablished
vectors.rationale: The card was read for the file alone after the token; an entry handing PPSSPP anything else is one the card does not answer for.

vectors.name: duckstation-a-chd-is-launchable-with-its-content-unread
vectors.rationale: DuckStation opens a .chd by its extension and then reads its header and tracks, which this card does not; the open reading of issue #716 reads no launched .chd, so the card answers.

vectors.name: duckstation-an-executable-is-launchable-with-its-content-unread
vectors.rationale: A .psexe boots as an executable, loaded at the BIOS's kernel-init hook, which shuts the system down where the load fails: the content decides, and atlas does not read it.

vectors.name: duckstation-a-zip-is-not-accepted-by-the-duckstation-entry
vectors.rationale: CDImage::Open answers a .zip 'Unknown extension': DuckStation opens no archive.

vectors.name: duckstation-an-mdf-is-not-accepted-by-the-duckstation-entry
vectors.rationale: A launched .mdf is refused, 'Unknown extension', although the .mds beside it opens it.

vectors.name: duckstation-a-ccd-depends-on-the-build
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK's DuckStation refuses a .ccd and the upstream build EmuDeck installs opens it, so neither a take nor a refusal holds on every machine the card serves.

vectors.name: duckstation-a-cue-keeps-the-open-reading
vectors.rationale: Where the open reading of issue #716 reads the launched file, it decides and the card is never asked: the verdict states what DuckStation opens and no card caveat.

vectors.name: duckstation-a-chd-handed-without-batch-stays-unestablished
vectors.rationale: The card was read for -batch %ROM%. The open reading also answers a bare %ROM%, but reads no .chd, and the card does not answer for that command.
